newsitem.title: KENYA: Denmark sees corruption, mismanagement in Kenya.
newsitem.headline: Denmark sees corruption, mismanagement in Kenya.

text.p: Denmark has cut its aid to Kenya because of corruption and the mismanagement of resources, Danish Minister for Development Cooperation Poul Nielsen told reporters in Nairobi.
Speaking after meeting government and opposition leaders, Nielsen said Danish aid had been halved since the 1980s to about $25 million this year.
"Mismanagement of resources and corruption are among the reasons for limiting Danish aid to Kenya," Nielsen said on Saturday night.
Although Kenya ended one-party rule in December 1991, the ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) party continued to dominate, he said.
"The distribution of authority reflects a dominance of the ruling party. We fear there still remain one-party state methods in public life here," Nielsen added.
He said he had met opposition politicians, who had complained of harassment which limited their effectiveness in preparing for elections due to take place this year.
During Nielsen's visit a group of opposition supporters said they had been beaten up by police after distributing leaflets calling for the respect of human rights in Kenya.
